hits.title: UK’s Financial Ombudsman Service annual review highlights increasing numbers of complaints
hits.snippet: It is a helpful insight into the work of FOS and industry trends.  Headlines   The volume of complaints increased significantly to 198,798 (up from 165,149 for the previous financial year).  Slight increase to the percentage of the complaints it upheld, increasing from 35% to 37%.  The top 5 products complained about are:   + Current accounts (30,635 complaints)   + Credit cards (24,402 complaints)   + Hire purchase (motor) (21,411 complaints)   + Car/motorcycle insurance (16,322 complaints) [...] complaints)   + Conditional sale (motor) (7,829 complaints)  Conditional sale (motor) is new to the top 5, overtaking insurance related complaints.  The total number of complaints received about banking and payments reaching a ten year high, with the overall uphold rate at 40%. FOS suggests that this rise is largely due to concerns about current accounts and credit cards, as well as complaints about fraud and scams.  Around half of the over 27,000 new fraud and scam cases related to Authorised [...] expected in Q3 of this year.  Unaffordable lending complaints continue to rise as a rapid pace, making up a large proportion of complaints in relation to credit cards (c13,000). Unaffordability complaints also appear in relation to other financial products (over c9,000 complaints).  There was an increase in complaints brought to FOS by claims management companies (“CMCs”) and other professional representatives to 25% (18% in the previous year). Overall, we received 305,726 new complaints in 2024/25, the highest level of complaints for six years.
 This is a 54% increase when compared to the 198,798 complaints reported in the previous year.
 Complaints saw significant rises, with complaints about some issues and products at their highest ever recorded level.
 The most complained about product was Hire Purchase (motor)

The total number of new complaints we received about travel insurance in the last financial year has reached the highest-level since the pandemic – with cases primarily driven by people dissatisfied with insurers declining their claims.

Overall, we received 4,466 new complaints in 2023/24, compared to 3,745 in the year before.

hits.title: Complaints data | FCA
hits.snippet:
Firm specific complaints data

Our firm-specific complaints data set is composed of submissions from approximately 290 individual firms reporting either 500 or more complaints within a 6-month period, or 1,000 or more complaints annually. The data is available in 2 formats via 8 sortable tables that can be searched and filtered on at firm-level and a downloadable Excel file that can be filtered by 5 product groups.

Aggregate (total) complaints data [...] # Complaints data

Transparency from firms on the number of complaints they receive is helpful for industry and consumers. Firms can compare their performance in the market and consumers have an additional source of information about the firms we regulate. Further complaints data may be obtained from the Financial Ombudsman Service.

15 May 2026 update

Following our investigation into a reporting anomaly in one firm’s complaints return, we have updated the H1 2025 and H2 2025 data. [...] We publish our complaints data every 6 months, around April and October. We provide firm-specific data for individual firms and aggregate, or total, data at market-level. These data sets include submissions from firms reporting 500 or more complaints within a 6-month period, or firms reporting 1,000 or more complaints in a year. Firms that meet these thresholds are obligated to publish complaints data on their websites. These complaints account for around 98% of all complaints that firms report
